name: A German occupational lump sum of a Swiss citizen in Zurich, entered as taxed in Germany: a capital benefit with the German tax credited
workings: Under Art. 18 of the Germany-Switzerland treaty an occupational pension of a Swiss resident is Switzerland's; Art. 19 keeps a public-service one in Germany only for a German citizen, and this person is Swiss only. So Switzerland taxes the lump sum although the plan says taxedIn: source, with a warning, and credits the 3,000.00 Germany charged.
Capital benefit 100,000.00. Federal: 1/5 of the tariff (2,684.44) = 536.8880.
Zurich: the rate on 1/20 (5,000) is below 2%, so 2%: simple tax 2,000.0000; cantonal 95% = 1,900.0000, communal 119% = 2,380.0000; personal tax 24.
The Swiss tax on it is 4,816.8880, so the 3,000.00 is credited in full. Total 4,816.8880 + 24 - 3,000 = 1,840.8880.
